name: Framer
look: Black canvas throughout with no light interludes, poster-grade negative tracking, white pill CTAs and oversized gradient spotlight cards.

hero.title: Design and ship in one place
hero.sub: A canvas that publishes. Draw the site, wire the interactions, press publish — and get a real CDN-hosted page rather than an export you have to rebuild.

features.title: Design tools that actually publish
features.sub: The gap between the mockup and the live site is the whole problem. This closes it.

items.title: Real interactions
items.body: Scroll effects, hover states and page transitions authored on the canvas and shipped exactly as designed — no handoff, no reimplementation, no drift between the file and the site.

items.title: Responsive by default
items.body: Breakpoints inherit, so a change at desktop propagates unless you override it.

items.title: Fast by construction
items.body: Images optimised, fonts subset, CSS generated. Median published site scores 98.

items.title: CMS built in
items.body: Collections, references and dynamic pages without a separate service.

items.title: Multiplayer
items.body: Cursors, comments and version history on the same canvas.

items.title: Publish anywhere
items.body: A custom domain, a staging URL, or an export of clean React components if you would rather take the code and go.

showcases.title: Authored once, shipped as-is
showcases.body: Scroll-linked effects, hover states and page transitions are built on the same canvas as the layout and published without reimplementation. The prototype and the site stop being two different artefacts that slowly disagree.
points: Scroll, hover and page transitions on canvas
No handoff step and no drift

showcases.title: Fast because of how it builds
showcases.body: Images are optimised and served responsively, fonts are subset to the glyphs actually used, and the CSS is generated from the canvas rather than accumulated by hand. The median published site scores 98 on Lighthouse.

gallery.title: Templates
gallery.sub: Fourteen hundred, all editable on the canvas and publishable in a click.

testimonial.quote: We shipped a marketing site in four days that would have been four weeks of design, handoff and front-end. The designer published it herself and nobody opened a code editor.
testimonial.name: Priya Anand

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.sub: Free while you build. Pay when you attach a domain.

items.q: Is it actually fast, or fast in a demo?
items.a: The median published site scores 98 on Lighthouse against real field data, not lab runs. The benchmarks page shows the distribution rather than just the median.

items.q: What happens to my site if I stop paying?
items.a: The custom domain stops resolving and the site reverts to its Loom subdomain. Nothing is deleted, and reattaching the domain restores it.

notes: The black canvas carries hero, body, pricing, FAQ and footer alike. There are no light interludes in this system.
Display tracking runs aggressively negative — around -5.5px at the largest size. That poster-grade cadence is the typographic signature.
The white pill is the only primary CTA shape on the site. Secondary actions are charcoal pills or plain text links.
Gradient spotlight cards are individual tiles inside the dark grid — never section backgrounds. Turning one into a band collapses the effect.
One chromatic accent is reserved for links, focus and selection. It is never decorative.
